verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 56.39
verses.english: Linked Discourses 56.39

verses.pali: 4. Sīsapāvanavagga
verses.english: 4. In a Rosewood Forest

verses.pali: Indakhīlasutta
verses.english: Indra’s pillar

verses.pali: “Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti …pe…
verses.english: “Mendicants, there are ascetics and brahmins who don’t truly understand about suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti, te aññassa samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā mukhaṁ ullokenti:
verses.english: They gaze up at the face of another ascetic or brahmin, thinking:

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ nūna bhavaṁ jānaṁ jānāti, passaṁ passatī’ti.
verses.english: ‘Surely this worthy one knows and sees.’

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, tūlapicu vā kappāsapicu vā lahuko vātūpādāno same bhūmibhāge nikkhitto.
verses.english: Suppose there was a light tuft of cotton-wool or kapok which was taken up by the wind and landed on level ground.

verses.pali: Tamenaṁ puratthimo vāto pacchimena saṁhareyya, pacchimo vāto puratthimena saṁhareyya, uttaro vāto dakkhiṇena saṁhareyya, dakkhiṇo vāto uttarena saṁhareyya.
verses.english: The east wind wafts it west; the west wind wafts it east; the north wind wafts it south; and the south wind wafts it north.

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Lahukattā, bhikkhave, kappāsapicuno.
verses.english: It’s because the tuft of cotton-wool is so light.

verses.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye hi keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti …pe…
verses.english: In the same way, there are ascetics and brahmins who don’t truly understand about suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti, te aññassa samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā mukhaṁ ullokenti:
verses.english: They gaze up at the face of another ascetic or brahmin, thinking:

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ nūna bhavaṁ jānaṁ jānāti, passaṁ passatī’ti.
verses.english: ‘Surely this worthy one knows and sees.’

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Adiṭṭhattā, bhikkhave, catunnaṁ ariyasaccānaṁ.
verses.english: It’s because they haven’t seen the four noble truths.

verses.pali: Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti …pe…
verses.english: There are ascetics and brahmins who truly understand about suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti, te na aññassa samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā mukhaṁ ullokenti:
verses.english: They don’t gaze up at the face of another ascetic or brahmin, thinking:

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ nūna bhavaṁ jānaṁ jānāti, passaṁ passatī’ti.
verses.english: ‘Surely this worthy one knows and sees.’

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ayokhīlo vā indakhīlo vā gambhīranemo sunikhāto acalo asampakampī.
verses.english: Suppose there was an iron pillar or an Indra’s pillar with deep foundations, firmly embedded, imperturbable and unshakable.

verses.pali: Puratthimāya cepi disāya āgaccheyya bhusā vātavuṭṭhi, neva saṅkampeyya na sampakampeyya na sampacāleyya; pacchimāya cepi disāya …pe… uttarāya cepi disāya …pe… dakkhiṇāya cepi disāya āgaccheyya bhusā vātavuṭṭhi, neva saṅkampeyya na sampakampeyya na sampacāleyya.
verses.english: Even if violent storms were to blow up out of the east, the west, the north, and the south, they couldn’t make it shake or rock or tremble.

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Gambhīrattā, bhikkhave, nemassa sunikhātattā indakhīlassa.
verses.english: It’s because that Indra’s pillar is firmly embedded, with deep foundations.

verses.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye ca kho keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti …pe…
verses.english: In the same way, there are ascetics and brahmins who truly understand about suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.

verses.pali: ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti, te na aññassa samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā mukhaṁ ullokenti:
verses.english: They don’t gaze up at the face of another ascetic or brahmin, thinking:

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ nūna bhavaṁ jānaṁ jānāti, passaṁ passatī’ti.
verses.english: ‘Surely this worthy one knows and sees.’

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Sudiṭṭhattā, bhikkhave, catunnaṁ ariyasaccānaṁ.
verses.english: It’s because they have clearly seen the four noble truths.

verses.pali: Katamesaṁ catunnaṁ?
verses.english: What four?

verses.pali: Dukkhassa ariyasaccassa …pe… dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ariyasaccassa.
verses.english: The noble truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.

verses.pali: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yogo karaṇīyo …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti.
verses.english: That’s why you should practice meditation …”

verses.pali: Navamaṁ.
